newsitem.title: USA: Miami Hispanic festival returns after hiatus.
newsitem.headline: Miami Hispanic festival returns after hiatus.

text.p: Miami's carnival, reputed to be the largest Hispanic street festival in North America, returned on Sunday after being cancelled last year when Cuba shot down two planes flown by Cuban exiles.

Thousands of people gathered along a two-mile stretch of Eighth Street -- from which the festival got its nickname, Calle Ocho -- in the heart of Little Havana for singing, dancing and Latin American cuisine. Organisers said they were expecting up to one million people to attend.
Organisers said they hoped to break the world record for most people dancing the Macarena. The record of 50,000 was set in 1995 at Yankee Stadium in New York.
In 1988, Carnaval Miami made the Guinness Book of Records for the world's largest conga line when 119,000 danced to the music of Miamian Gloria Estefan.

The festival, put on by the local Kiwanis Club, was cancelled last year as the Cuban-American community mourned the deaths of four members of the exile group Brothers to the Rescue, whose planes were shot down by Cuban MiG fighters on Feb. 24 over the Florida Straits.
